title: Human-Object Interaction from Human-Level Instructions
summary: Language planning orchestrates contextual full-body manipulation with finger interactions and RL reference tracking.
limitations: Reference-conditioned physics tracking is not a general reference-free policy. Future target/path conditions are supplied; environmental perception remains a future-work direction.
method: LLM scene planning and A* navigation feed CoarseNet; predicted contact phases drive grasp generation, wrist-relative RefineNet and FingerNet. RL separately tracks the generated reference.
conditions: Full system: instruction, scene/assets and initial states. Low-level CoarseNet additionally requires final object pose and 2D waypoints every 30 frames; planner-generated conditions must be distinguished from GT-extracted paths.
evaluation: FullBodyManipulation low-level comparisons include CHOIS+GRIP; waypoint, foot, hand/object contact, intersection and pose metrics plus perception study; physics tracker is evaluated separately.

title: Surface Keypoint Representation for Multi-Object and Articulated Human-Object Interaction Generation
summary: Represents rigid components with surface-keypoint trajectories, predicts spatiotemporal contact-distance fields and synthesizes contact-guided whole-body motion.
limitations: Authors report remaining floating/penetration. Contact optimization costs approximately four minutes per 124 frames; geometric representation is not force/dynamics certification.
method: Three transformer/flow-matching stages generate rigid-component keypoints, contact-distance fields and body markers; inference optimizes body diffusion noise against contact and object-SDF penetration losses.
conditions: Text, object BPS geometry and initial human/object state; alternatives supply sparse object waypoints or full future object trajectories. Main generated object paths are predictions, not automatically GT.
evaluation: ParaHome, HIMO, ARCTIC and OMOMO; FID, text alignment, foot sliding, interaction geometry/contact and object jerk; representation/contact ablations.
evidence_locator: §§3.1–3.2; 4.1–4.4; Appendix B metrics and G failure cases

title: DuetHOI: Language-Guided Bimanual Hand--Object Motion Generation with Articulation Planning and Contact Refinement
summary: Contact intent and articulation planning condition structured hand/object generation; proximity refinement fixes objects while correcting hands.
limitations: One articulation scalar and one instruction at a time; explicitly excludes coupled joints and inter-task transitions. Phy/contact metrics do not establish executed physics. Same arXiv identity as earlier StructBiHOI revisions.
method: ContactVAE samples contact intent; conditional-prior ArtPlanner predicts scalar articulation, ManiVAE compresses hands, and DualFormer couples token/time streams. ProxiRefine corrects hands while fixing generated object motion.
conditions: Language, canonical geometry and initial articulation. ArtPlanner’s test reference is predicted from its conditional prior; its training posterior sees GT articulation. This is hand/object generation, without locomotion.
evaluation: ARCTIC articulated/rigid and one/two-hand modes; GRAB rigid modes; adapted Text2HOI, LatentHOI and MDM; contact, hand/object errors, diversity and relative consistency; component/refinement ablations.
evidence_locator: Method: Articulation Trajectory Planning, Token-Temporal Interaction Generation, Object-Fixed Hand Refinement; Experiments; Conclusion: Limitations

title: ReMoS: 3D Motion-Conditioned Reaction Synthesis for Two-Person Interactions
summary: Spatiotemporal cross-attention generates a second person’s body and hand response to a given actor motion; contributes ReMoCap.
limitations: Fast contact-heavy sequences can misalign spatially, motivating guidance. Proximity-based hand masks do not establish actual physical contact or force feasibility.
method: Cascaded diffusion first generates reactive body joints using joint spatiotemporal cross-attention, then hands with proximity-derived interaction masks; reaction/kinematic losses and inference guidance improve alignment.
conditions: Complete actor body/hand motion over the target interval is supplied. Reactor motion is generated; this is future actor-conditioned completion rather than two-person generation from text or causal online reaction.
evaluation: ReMoCap Lindy Hop/Ninjutsu, 2C and ExPI; MPJPE/velocity error, body/hand FID, diversity, ablations and user study; appendix adds InterHuman comparisons.

method: Trajectory diffusion generates human/object paths; action diffusion then conditions densely on these predicted positions. Distal-joint adversarial training and reconstruction guidance target contact and grounded feet.
conditions: Text, object BPS geometry, first human/object poses and final object position. Intermediate waypoints are not prescribed. Action-stage paths are TG predictions; Appendix E.3 separately gives all-frame GT paths as an oracle.
evaluation: FullBodyManipulation and unseen same-category 3D-FUTURE geometry; condition/contact/motion/GT errors, ablations, perception study and DynaPlan dynamic planning.
limitations: Rigid-object scope; DynaPlan supports one manipulated object and one moving obstacle. No explicit physical simulation guarantee; articulated/deformable dynamics remain future work.
title: Decoupled Generative Modeling for Human-Object Interaction Synthesis
summary: DecHOI separates goal-conditioned trajectory planning from contact-oriented action generation.

title: PrimHOI: Compositional Human-Object Interaction via Reusable Primitives
summary: Composes relative-geometry interaction primitives spatially and temporally through hierarchical planning, targeting unseen multi-object tasks.
limitations: Evidence here is the author’s method overview, not a completed full-paper audit. Linked official repository exposes only README/LICENSE as checked; its URL does not establish released runnable implementation.
method: Author method overview: LLM compiles a task into PDDL-HOI; symbolic planning yields subgoal graphs. Primitive contact factors generate key poses; object paths precede contact-guided intermediate human motion and constraint post-optimization.
conditions: Task description, scene/object geometry and symbolic domain knowledge; planned subgoals and object/contact trajectories are internal generated conditions, not a claim of text+initial-state-only direct diffusion.
evaluation: Official page demonstrates four primitive contact modes, varied shapes/placements and three extended plans. Detailed quantitative evaluation was not re-audited because CVF PDF fetch returned 403.
evidence_locator: Author page: Method Overview, The Three Long Plans, Results; CVF abstract. Full PDF inaccessible via browser tool.
code_status: official linked placeholder: only README/LICENSE observed
